offers_products.reason: Owns and leases open-air shopping centers; no manufactured goods or software sold.

offers_services.reason: REIT leasing and managing retail properties to tenants; REITs count as services.

sells_to_consumers.reason: Tenants are retailers and businesses leasing space in shopping centers, not households.

sells_to_organizations.reason: Leases space to retail tenants such as grocers, restaurants and national retail chains.

recurring_revenue.reason: Rental income from multi-year leases with retail tenants.

cyclical_demand.reason: Tenants are bound by multi-year leases; convenience-oriented open-air centers are relatively resilient, though retail tenants can fail.

big_ticket.reason: Monthly rent payments under leases are small and frequent relative to tenants' spending.

people_delivered.reason: Revenue comes from owned shopping center properties, not staff time.

large_customers.reason: Tenants are a mix of national chains and many small shops; not mainly large enterprises or government.

asset_heavy.reason: REIT owning open-air shopping center properties requiring ongoing property investment.

notes: Tenant size mix inferred from the open-air shopping center model; website text is brief.
